subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw pursue first-class multi-index memorySearch with new config, storage, migration, and status contracts, or keep the current single-index identity guard plus narrower fallback repairs?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a mechanical bug fix; it introduces new public config, persistent index semantics, provider-routing policy, and operator-facing recovery surfaces that repository policy treats as product/API decisions.

options.title: Sponsor multi-index design
options.body: Keep this issue open and have a maintainer define the per-model index API, migration/doctor path, status output, and fallback policy before implementation.

options.title: Limit to single-index safeguards
options.body: Defer multi-index failover and continue shipping only scalar provider/model identity guards plus explicit rebuild behavior.

options.title: Prioritize narrow fallback bugs
options.body: Use this issue as future design context while landing bounded fixes such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534 independently.

recommendation.title: Sponsor multi-index design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have a maintainer define the per-model index API, migration/doctor path, status output, and fallback policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is assigned on the live issue and authored the current memory index identity and local embedding fallback work most directly adjacent to the decision.
